topics.title: Mendel's experiments and inheritance of one gene

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Mendel used true-breeding pea lines with seven pairs of contrasting traits to study inheritance.
Work out the phenotypic and genotypic ratios of a monohybrid cross using the laws of dominance and segregation.
Use a test cross with the recessive parent to find the genotype of a plant showing the dominant phenotype.

topics.title: Incomplete dominance, co-dominance and multiple alleles

concepts.learning_objective: Explain incomplete dominance with the snapdragon flower colour example and its 1:2:1 F2 ratio.
Explain co-dominance using the ABO blood group alleles and work out possible blood groups of offspring.
Explain why multiple alleles of a gene can be recognised only through population studies.

topics.title: Inheritance of two genes and the chromosomal theory

concepts.learning_objective: Derive the 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratio and apply the law of independent assortment to gamete and offspring calculations.
Relate the behaviour of chromosomes in meiosis to Mendel's laws as proposed by Sutton and Boveri.
Explain how linkage of genes on the same chromosome changes dihybrid ratios and how recombination arises.
Use recombination frequency as a measure of the distance between genes on a chromosome.
Explain the additive effect of alleles in polygenic traits such as human skin colour.
Explain how a single gene such as the one mutated in phenylketonuria can show multiple phenotypic effects.
Compare XO, XY and ZW mechanisms of sex determination and the ideas of male and female heterogamety.
Explain why the sperm decides the sex of a human child and why each birth has a 50 per cent chance of either sex.
Describe the haplodiploid sex-determination system of the honey bee and its consequences.
Distinguish point mutations, frame-shift mutations and chromosomal aberrations and identify mutagens.
Use pedigree analysis to infer whether a human trait is dominant or recessive, autosomal or sex-linked.
Predict the inheritance of X-linked recessive disorders such as colour blindness and haemophilia.
Explain the genetic basis of sickle-cell anaemia, phenylketonuria and thalassemia.
Relate Down's, Klinefelter's and Turner's syndromes to aneuploidy and their karyotypes.
